skill.name: blender-game-optimization
skill.description: Optimize Blender assets for real-time engines - triangle/material/texture/bone budgets per platform (mobile, Roblox, web, VR, console, PC), LOD chains, decimation modes, mesh cleanup, draw-call reduction (material merging, atlases, trim sheets), instancing, vertex-split costs, collision proxies, texture memory. Use when an asset is too heavy, before export, or when targeting a platform budget.
skill.summary: Measure Blender assets against platform budgets and generate lower-detail meshes for real-time engines.
skill.author: el4cteo

security_audit.summary: All 25 static matches are false positives: they refer to Blender documentation, local Blender commands, or Blender data. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, system reconnaissance, or data exfiltration. LOD generation can delete existing scene objects with matching names, and omitted object names can broaden the operation.

remediation.issue: LOD generation can replace existing scene objects without verifying ownership or asking for confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Check all target names before editing and stop on collisions by default. Require explicit replacement approval and limit replacement to LODs linked to the source mesh.

remediation.issue: Omitting object names can expand a modifying operation from the selection to all visible meshes.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit object names for LOD generation and show the planned edits before running. Document the cleanup, rename, and save effects, and recommend a separate output file.

semantic_findings.title: LOD Generation Can Remove Existing Scene Objects
semantic_findings.description: The documented LOD workflow does not warn about name collisions. The generator deletes existing objects with matching LOD names without checking ownership or asking for confirmation. Without object names, the shared selector can include all visible meshes. Saving the changed scene can make unintended deletions permanent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reviewed generator deletes objects by matching name before creating replacements. The shared selector explicitly falls back to visible meshes when no eligible objects are selected.

content.user_title: Optimize Blender Assets for Real-Time Games
content.value_statement: Dense meshes and large textures can put game assets over their performance budgets. Measure Blender assets against platform guidance and create lower-detail meshes for review before export.
actual_capabilities: Count vertices and triangles on selected or named meshes after Blender evaluates their modifiers.
Report materials, estimated draw calls, image dimensions, estimated uncompressed texture memory, and rig bone counts.
Flag assets that exceed preset guidance for mobile, Roblox, web, VR, console, or PC.
Generate lower-detail mesh copies with configurable decimation ratios and optional symmetry.
Optionally merge nearby vertices, dissolve degenerate geometry, and remove loose vertices before generating lower-detail meshes.
Suggest ways to reduce material, texture, rig, and collision costs.
limitations: The bundled scripts require Blender's Python environment.
Budget presets are guidance. Draw calls and texture memory are estimates, not engine measurements.
Generated meshes need visual checks for silhouette changes and UV damage. The scripts do not export assets or configure engine LOD switching.
LOD generation can replace existing objects with matching names. Cleanup and renaming can also modify the source asset.

use_cases.title: Check a mobile prop budget
use_cases.description: Measure a prop before export and identify whether geometry, materials, or texture size exceeds the mobile preset.

use_cases.title: Build lower-detail environment meshes
use_cases.description: Generate three lower-detail meshes from a named environment asset and compare triangle counts and silhouettes.

use_cases.title: Review assets for standalone VR
use_cases.description: Compare mesh, material, and texture metrics against the VR preset to choose assets for device profiling.

prompt_templates.title: Measure one prop
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect a named asset before making changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Measure the crate mesh against the mobile budget without changing or saving the scene. Explain each item that exceeds the preset.

prompt_templates.title: Plan reductions for a web asset
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: choose changes from a budget report.
prompt_templates.prompt: Measure the kiosk mesh against the web preset. Rank geometry, material, and texture changes by their likely visual impact. Do not apply the changes.

prompt_templates.title: Generate an LOD chain on a copy
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: create lower-detail versions of one prop.
prompt_templates.prompt: In a duplicate scene file, check for existing LOD names for the rock mesh and stop if any match. Generate levels at 50%, 25%, and 12.5%. Report the triangle counts and flag areas to inspect for UV or silhouette changes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare LOD results before export
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare measured geometry with a project target.
prompt_templates.prompt: Measure the original antenna and its lower-detail meshes separately against the VR preset. Compare triangle counts, materials, and estimated texture memory. Explain what must be verified on the target device before export.

output_examples.input: Check the crate against the mobile prop budget.
output: The crate has 4,800 triangles, above the 3,000-triangle mobile prop guideline.
Its two materials meet the preset. Its 2,048-pixel image exceeds the 1,024-pixel texture guideline.
Try reducing hidden geometry and checking whether a 1,024-pixel image preserves enough detail.

output_examples.input: Summarize the lower-detail versions of the rock mesh.
output: The source has 8,000 triangles. The three lower-detail meshes have about 4,000, 2,000, and 1,000 triangles.
Compare their silhouettes and UV seams before choosing where each level should appear in the engine.

best_practices: Use a duplicate blend file and check generated names for collisions before making changes.
Pass explicit object names and measure the same asset before and after optimization.
Review silhouettes and UV seams, then profile the exported asset in the target engine.
anti_patterns: Running LOD generation without object names in a scene with many visible meshes.
Enabling cleanup on the only copy of a source asset.
Treating estimated draw calls and preset budgets as measured engine performance.

faq.question: Do the scripts run outside Blender?
faq.answer: No. They use Blender's Python API and require Blender, either in an interactive session or in background mode.

faq.question: Which platforms have budget presets?
faq.answer: The statistics script includes mobile, Roblox, web, standalone VR, console, and PC presets.

faq.question: Are the budget presets hard limits?
faq.answer: No. They are per-asset guidelines. Check current platform requirements and profile the complete scene on the target device.

faq.question: Does the statistics script save my file?
faq.answer: No. It measures the scene and does not accept a save option. It can switch Blender to Object Mode before measuring.

faq.question: Can LOD generation overwrite an existing object?
faq.answer: Yes. It removes objects that already use a generated LOD name. Work on a duplicate file and check the names before running it.

faq.question: Does the skill export the generated meshes?
faq.answer: No. The bundled tools measure meshes and generate LOD objects. Export and engine configuration are separate steps.
